supersedes_run: temporal_gitlab pilot of 2026-10-19T02:20 (archived, contributes no reported number)
written_before: the first formal GitLab transition; the pilot is archived and none of its cells enter any denominator

finding_that_forces_the_change.cell: T4 group_member_remove, object acme/t1, subject bob, action read
finding_that_forces_the_change.pilot_result: E=allow (ledger still held the direct project grant), Y=deny (HTTP 404 on the raw file)
finding_that_forces_the_change.state_evidence: after the group removal, GET /projects/{acme/t1}/members returned an empty direct-member list (before: bob was listed), while GET /projects/{acme/t1}/members/all returned only dave
finding_that_forces_the_change.interpretation: GitLab deletes a user's direct project membership in the group's projects when that user's group membership is removed. This is a non-local side effect of an out-of-band mutation: the harness never issued a project-level revoke.

why_not_model_it_in_the_ledger: Encoding the rule would make E depend on a behaviour we learned by observing the product, which is the exact failure mode the A-package removed (Y leaking into E).
The rule is not stated in the GitLab group-management documentation we could retrieve, so it could not be cited as a documented inheritance rule.
A ledger that silently mutates rows the harness never touched would also misrepresent what an external auditor can know.

change.topology: the alternative-channel object for T4 moves outside the group namespace: dave/r4 is a personal project with a direct grant to bob. acme/t1 keeps only the group channel.
change.expected_effect: T4 now tests 'one channel removed, another channel retained' without touching any product rule about cascading membership deletion.
change.scored_run: fresh container and fresh volume; all eight transitions are re-executed from an empty topology.

side_observation_to_report.claim: an out-of-band group mutation removed a project-level membership that no transaction in the harness listed
side_observation_to_report.evidence: state query before/after, recorded in this file and in the pilot archive
side_observation_to_report.status: reported as a product-semantics note in the paper; not used to compute E and not counted as a violation

oracle_note.expected_disagreements: GET /projects/{id}/members/all/{uid} answers membership, not entitlement: it returns 404 for a public project a non-member may read, and for a site administrator who may read everything. O will therefore disagree with E on those cells.
oracle_note.handling: O stays a reported column; it never sets E, TP or FP. The disagreement count is a measured fidelity property, reported per system.
